title: Sanctions Gain Teeth
summary:
Sanctions Gain Teeth
With the enactment of a new U.S. sanctions regime earlier this month, the tanker industry has once again found itself drawn directly into the fray surrounding Iran. On July 1 st , President Obama signed the Comprehensive Iran Sanctions, Accountability, and Divestment Act of 2010, imposing further restrictions on business dealings with Iran.

children.title: Targeting Tankers
children.summary: An exception for underwriters and insurance providers who have practiced due diligence in establishing procedures to comply with the prohibition was included in the law. Ongoing efforts to isolate Tehran are, nonetheless, having an effect on the ability to secure insurance for refined product imports into Iran.

children.title: Trade Flows Frozen?
children.summary: A Government Accountability Office report earlier this year named companies actively involved in trading gasoline into Iran and subsequent pressure on these companies forced most to relent and end their supply contracts. Throughout 2010, they have been joined by a procession of companies including Eni, Total, and Reliance which have announced that they would end business dealings with Iran.

children.title: 2010 YTD
children.summary: Negotiations to reconcile different versions of the sanctions bill reportedly focused on the need for flexibility in light of the effort to gather support for United Nations sanctions against Iran. To help provide this flexibility, the law allows for a one‐year waiver for companies found in violation that are closely cooperating with multilateral efforts against Iran.
